</role>
<definition>
Question: is every claim in the brief supported by the cited evidence and the fact sheet, with nothing overstated and no cited contrary evidence left out? Pass means yes.
Fail on an uncited claim, a number that is off the fact sheet, a scope wider than the cited accounts, a paraphrase placed in quotation marks, or an ignored contrary citation.
The evidence is the brief, the cited insights and the fact sheet (accounts, ARR, mentions, routes, renewals).
</definition>

 "brief": "## Problem\n\nGarage estimates uploaded to Keelwater are being filed under the wrong document category, typically Correspondence, and handlers must manually recategorise them. The misfiling causes delays and creates a risk that critical evidence is overlooked during claims processing [i:0fc6cb6155656fe2] [i:10727c617a1f4506].\n\n## Who is affected\n\n- Handlers at Linnet House Insurance are still manually moving garage estimates out of correspondence, which is causing delays [i:33fbb6b3d920009b].\n- Handlers at Saltmarsh Specialty are spending too much time fixing incorrect file type assignments and need a better way to classify garage estimates so critical evidence is not missed during claims processing [i:35bc60912c19d67e].\n- Handlers at Brackwater Homecover keep missing key evidence because uploaded garage estimates land in the wrong document category, which delays claims resolution [i:a3f2a53f98cd8130].\n- Handlers at Marrowgate Commercial have to manually move garage estimates that land under Correspondence, which risks things slipping through the cracks [i:766f9ca2be319649].\n- Handlers at Cindermill Trade Cover have to move misfiled garage estimates manually, which risks missing critical evidence [i:d8352b80a8797730].\n- Handlers at Thistlecombe Mutual are affected by the document upload system assigning the wrong category, such as putting repair quotes under correspondence, leading to incorrect file type issues [i:f51ad41373d3cadc].\n\n## Evidence\n\n- Across 6 accounts, 14 mentions and 3 routes, this issue appears in account_management (3 mentions), support (8 mentions) and onboarding (3 mentions); the affected accounts represent 4500000.0 GBP in ARR, with 1 renewal in the next 90 days [i:0fc6cb6155656fe2] [i:10727c617a1f4506] [i:71de0c62620ee6ab].\n- Linnet House Insurance (360000.0 GBP ARR, renewal 2027-03-14, 4 mentions) reports that every time a garage estimate gets dumped into correspondence, someone has to manually fix it, and sometimes the wrong document category means evidence gets overlooked entirely [i:0fc6cb6155656fe2].\n- Saltmarsh Specialty (740000.0 GBP ARR, renewal 2027-05-15, 4 mentions) reports that garage estimates keep landing in correspondence, requiring manual recategorisation, and that the incorrect file type assignment is causing real delays and oversight risks [i:10727c617a1f4506].\n- Brackwater Homecover (610000.0 GBP ARR, renewal 2027-10-10, 2 mentions) reports that every time a garage estimate is uploaded it lands in correspondence, and handlers keep missing key evidence because of it [i:3fa3eaf44b4d7c2f].\n- Marrowgate Commercial (1600000.0 GBP ARR, renewal 2026-12-12, 2 mentions) reports that uploaded garage estimates land in the wrong document category, such as under Correspondence, and have to be moved manually, which risks things slipping through the cracks [i:766f9ca2be319649].\n- Cindermill Trade Cover (210000.0 GBP ARR, renewal 2027-04-03, 1 mention) reports that uploaded documents sometimes end up misfiled, with garage estimates tagged as correspondence and handlers moving them manually, which risks missing critical evidence [i:d8352b80a8797730].\n- Thistlecombe Mutual (980000.0 GBP ARR, renewal 2027-09-01, 1 mention) reports that the document upload system keeps assigning the wrong category, such as putting repair quotes under correspondence, which leads to incorrect file type issues [i:f51ad41373d3cadc].\n- A cited insight points the other way: Marrowgate Commercial also reported handlers being locked out with Keelwater is down messages that were actually caused by their own customer network failure, and that the Claims Tasks panel moved without warning [i:71de0c62620ee6ab].\n\n## Why now\n\n- Marrowgate Commercial, representing 1600000.0 GBP in ARR, renews on 2026-12-12, which is 1 renewal within the next 90 days as of 2026-11-03 [i:766f9ca2be319649].\n- The issue is reported across 3 routes, including onboarding (3 mentions), so new accounts are encountering the misfiling during setup [i:d8352b80a8797730] [i:71de0c62620ee6ab].\n- Support carries the highest volume of mentions at 8, indicating handlers are repeatedly raising the same misfiling problem after go-live [i:10727c617a1f4506] [i:58f25c7f0bd10654].\n",

response.content: {"critique": "I checked every account-level claim against the cited insights and the fact sheet: ARR figures (360k, 740k, 610k, 1.6m, 210k, 980k, total 4.5m), renewal dates, mention counts (14 total, 4/4/2/2/1/1), and route breakdown (3 account_management, 8 support, 3 onboarding) all match exactly. Each 'who is affected' bullet is a faithful paraphrase of its cited quote, with no paraphrase placed in quotation marks, and no scope widened beyond the cited accounts. The contrary Marrowgate insight (network-failure lockouts and the moved Claims Tasks panel) is explicitly surfaced in the Evidence section rather than omitted. The 'why now' claims (Marrowgate renewal 2026-12-12 within 90 days of 2026-11-03, onboarding mentions indicating setup-stage encounters, support carrying the highest volume) are all supported by the cited insights and fact sheet.", "verdict": "pass"}
